question: A marketer runs a new campaign chat each week and re-pastes the same brand guidelines and tone-of-voice document into every one. She wants to stop repeating herself. Which sequence of steps is correct?
options: A) Add project instructions; run each campaign chat inside it; create a Project; upload the guidelines as project knowledge.
B) Upload the guidelines as project knowledge; run each campaign chat inside it; create a Project; add project instructions.
C) Create a Project; upload the guidelines as project knowledge; add project instructions; run each campaign chat inside it.
D) Run each campaign chat first; add project instructions; create a Project; upload the guidelines as project knowledge.
correct_answers: C) Create a Project; upload the guidelines as project knowledge; add project instructions; run each campaign chat inside it.
explanations: Incorrect. Instructions and chats are both scoped to a project, so neither can come before the project is created.
Incorrect. Knowledge is uploaded into a project, so the upload cannot precede creating one, and the chats would run without the instructions.
Correct. The workspace has to exist before knowledge and instructions can be attached to it, and the chats only inherit that context once they are started inside the finished project.
Incorrect. The campaign chats would run before the guidelines and instructions are in place, so the early work gets none of the benefit, and instructions cannot be added before the project exists.
